A steel rule can be read to the nearest millimetre. It is used to measure the length of a bar whose
true length is 895 mm. Repeated measurements give the following readings.
length / mm
892, 891, 892, 891, 891, 892
Are the readings accurate and precise to within 1 mm?
results are precise
results are accurate
to within 1 mm
to within 1 mm
A
no
no
B
no
yes
C
yes
no
D
yes
yes

hints: Notice the true length is $895\text{ mm}$ while the six repeated readings are only $891\text{ mm}$ or $892\text{ mm}$.
Recall that accuracy is closeness of a reading to the true value, while precision is closeness of the repeated readings to each other.
Check the two gaps separately against $1\text{ mm}$: the $895\text{ mm}$ minus reading gap for accuracy, and the $892\text{ mm}$ minus $891\text{ mm}$ spread for precision.
walkthrough: State the rules: accurate means close to the true value of $895\text{ mm}$, precise means the repeated values agree closely with each other.
Check precision from the spread: maximum reading $892\text{ mm}$ minus minimum reading $891\text{ mm}$ is $1\text{ mm}$, so the set repeats to within $1\text{ mm}$.
Check accuracy from the error: $895 - 892 = 3\text{ mm}$ and $895 - 891 = 4\text{ mm}$, so every reading is $3\text{ mm}$ to $4\text{ mm}$ low.
Compare each result with the $1\text{ mm}$ limit: $1\text{ mm}$ spread passes for precision, but $3\text{ mm}$ to $4\text{ mm}$ error fails for accuracy.
The combination is results are not accurate to within $1\text{ mm}$ but are precise to within $1\text{ mm}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: It is wrong to say not precise, because all readings $891\text{ mm}$ to $892\text{ mm}$ lie within a $1\text{ mm}$ spread.

B.explanation: Readings cluster within $1\text{ mm}$ of each other but are $3\text{ mm}$ to $4\text{ mm}$ below the true $895\text{ mm}$, so not accurate but precise.

C.explanation: It is wrong to say accurate, because $895 - 892 = 3\text{ mm}$ and $895 - 891 = 4\text{ mm}$, both larger than $1\text{ mm}$.

D.explanation: It is wrong to say accurate, because the systematic shift of about $3\text{ mm}$ to $4\text{ mm}$ from $895\text{ mm}$ exceeds $1\text{ mm}$.
